name: Centaur
summary: Centaur clans still roam central Kalimdor, where they once drove the tauren close to extinction. Their line began with Zaetar and Theradras, and the Horde's arrival changed the course of their war with the tauren.

sections.title: A Cursed Lineage
sections.body: Centaur legend begins in Maraudon, beneath Desolace. Zaetar was an immortal son of the demigod Cenarius. Princess Theradras was daughter of Therazane, the elemental lord. Together they sired the first centaur. Soon after they emerged, the barbaric offspring turned on Zaetar and killed him. Grief-stricken, Theradras trapped his spirit in Maraudon's winding caverns. She shielded her vicious children as they multiplied across Kalimdor.

sections.title: Centuries of Slaughter
sections.body: From Desolace, centaur spread across Kalimdor and waged brutal war against its native peoples. The nomadic tauren suffered most. Driven from their fertile ancestral home in Mulgore, they fled across the Barrens as centaur warbands burned their settlements and hunted them for sport. By the Third War, centuries of pursuit had brought the tauren near extinction. They fled the endless marauders across the savannah.

sections.title: The Tide Turns
sections.body: The balance shifted when Warchief Thrall and the newly arrived orcish Horde landed on Kalimdor. Thrall made a pact with Cairne Bloodhoof. Orcish steel joined with tauren might, and together they crushed the aggressive Kolkar warbands and broke their hold on the plains. The tauren could safely establish Thunder Bluff and reclaim Mulgore. Their exile ended, and a debt of blood and honor bound them to the Horde.

sections.title: A Fractured Menace
sections.body: Centaur remain a threat across central Kalimdor despite their defeats. Their society is divided among warring clans, chiefly the Kolkar, Gelkis, Magram, and Maraudine. Each follows a khan, and the clans feud over territory and water. Their infighting keeps them from uniting. Yet raiding parties still strike trade caravans and settlements across Durotar, the Barrens, Thousand Needles, and the borders of Mulgore.

faq.answer: Centaur legend traces their birth to Zaetar, son of Cenarius, and Princess Theradras, daughter of Therazane, the elemental lord. The first centaur killed Zaetar, and Theradras trapped his spirit in Maraudon's caverns.

faq.q: Why do centaur hate the tauren so much?
faq.answer: Centaur spread from Desolace and raided the plains' native peoples for generations. They hunted the tauren for sport and drove them from Mulgore into exile across the Barrens. Before the orcs intervened, the tauren stood near extinction.

faq.q: What clans do the centaur belong to?
faq.answer: The main centaur clans on Kalimdor are the Kolkar, Gelkis, Magram, Maraudine, and Galak. Each traces its leadership to its founding khan, and the clans often fight bloody feuds.
Centaur territory centers on Desolace, where Maraudon lies. Warbands and outposts also roam the Barrens, Durotar, and Thousand Needles.

faq.q: Can centaur be reasoned or allied with?
faq.answer: Centaur generally see other races as prey to enslave or destroy. Rivalries between clans can be turned against them. In Desolace, the Magram or Gelkis have sometimes accepted outsider help to destroy their hated kin.

faq.q: Who is Princess Theradras to the centaur?
faq.answer: Princess Theradras is the centaur's mother and revered patron. In Maraudon, she protects the spirit of Zaetar, their murdered father. At times she has infused her descendants with elemental fury to spur them to conquer more territory across Kalimdor.

angles.text: As a tauren, you know centaur as the ancient tormentors who nearly wiped out your ancestors and drove them across the Barrens for centuries. The Horde offered salvation.
As a member of the Horde, defending against centaur incursions in the Barrens and Durotar means survival. It also honors the pact Thrall made with Cairne Bloodhoof.
As a druid, you see centaur as a tragic perversion of nature's balance. They share blood with Cenarius through his fallen son Zaetar, yet bring desolation and slaughter.
